author: WP17
summary: Alpha.1-era chapter on the easy-gl/meta-gl stack: ownership split, WebGL-aware initialization, the per-feature table, meta-gl's typed surface and terminate contract, API corrections, RAII helpers, two context-loss tiers, mock-loader tests, limitations and the history rewrite. Its pins (0b46d35c/571d3a62) are too old for 009d40f5 (Rgba16, exception model), CNA does not use Device::supports/require, DesktopEsTier is internal and CNA itself adopts RecoverableResource. libcna.com had only a sibling summary and CNA-side EasyGL internals; the library layer is now one deep dive.

concepts.section: easy-gl and meta-gl: Profile, Loader, and Dispatch
concepts.text: easy-gl is the C++ OpenGL/OpenGL ES wrapper behind CNA's five shared-family GL identities (OPENGLES2, OPENGLES3, OPENGL33, WEBGL1, WEBGL2); the family uses a two-library stack in which meta-gl owns loading, typed calls, context facts and validation and easy-gl owns resources and RAII.

concepts.section: The ownership split
concepts.text: easy-gl's 'toolkit-independent' means independent of the windowing toolkit, not of every layer below it: it is built on meta-gl, which provides a procedural, typed, ownership-free call surface (enum classes, typed handles, no RAII), and meta-gl's own notes say ownership belongs in easy-gl.

concepts.section: The ownership split
concepts.text: The easy-gl to meta-gl dependency is hard in build and source: easy-gl adds ../meta-gl and links meta-gl::meta-gl PUBLIC, and 18 production files (3 public headers, 15 sources) include meta-gl headers directly.

target.evidence: easy-gl@deda7a42:CMakeLists.txt (add_subdirectory(../meta-gl), target_link_libraries PUBLIC); git grep -l 'metagl/' deda7a4 -- include src

concepts.note: Extension recorded on the page: CNA also calls 44 distinct metagl::gl* wrappers directly from EasyGLRenderer.cpp.

concepts.section: The ownership split
concepts.text: Neither library creates a window or GL context, pumps events or presents; the host makes a context current and supplies a GetProcAddress callback. In CNA that host role is the selected platform (SDL3, SDL2, X11, Wayland, Win32; the browser under Emscripten), not SDL alone.
concepts.note: The unit says CNA fills the host role through SDL; at 009d40f5 native X11, Wayland and Win32 platforms also supply GL contexts.

concepts.section: The ownership split
concepts.text: The procedural lower layer is the larger one: easy-gl has 30 public headers and meta-gl 12, but by physical lines in include/ and src/ easy-gl is 4,449 and meta-gl 12,581 at the revisions read (older code-line counts 3,606 and about 8,856 show the same inversion).

target.evidence: git show <rev>:<file> | wc -l over include/ and src/ at easy-gl@deda7a42 and meta-gl@20c8b2dc

concepts.note: Recounted by physical lines; the unit quoted cloc code lines for the 2026-08-07 trees.

concepts.section: Device initialization delegates context truth downward
concepts.text: easygl::Device is the largest class: clear (incl. clear_buffer forms), viewport/scissor, blend state with per-draw-buffer overloads for MRT, depth/stencil, culling, polygon offset, line width, sample coverage and mask, pixel store, read_pixels and bounds-checked read_pixels_robust, the draw family (instanced, indirect, ranged, base-vertex), compute dispatch, set_patch_vertices and debug groups/labels/callback.
concepts.note: Polygon (line) mode is not a Device member at deda7a42; CNA detects the native wireframe API itself.

concepts.section: Device initialization delegates context truth downward
concepts.text: easy-gl no longer parses GL_VERSION itself: Device::initialize calls metagl::Initialize and copies GetContextInfo() and GetCapabilities() into its own Capabilities before running detect_common_features(); a null loader or a failed bootstrap throws, and initialize is one-shot.
concepts.note: Because initialize is one-shot, CNA reloads meta-gl directly on context restore (EasyGLRenderer.cpp).

concepts.section: Device initialization delegates context truth downward
concepts.text: meta-gl classifies Emscripten contexts as ApiKind::WebGL, so WebGL no longer passes for native OpenGL ES merely because its version string is ES-shaped; WebGL 1 is reported as 2.0 and WebGL 2 as 3.0 so one ES comparison serves both.

concepts.section: Device initialization delegates context truth downward
concepts.text: meta-gl's DesktopEsTier (the ES tier whose mandatory functions a desktop 3.3+ context also supplies) is an internal diagnostic at 20c8b2dc (metagl::detail, excluded from metagl.hpp, outside API/ABI guarantees); Capabilities::gles30/31/32 stay false on desktop, CNA never references it, and OPENGL33 shares CNA's implementation through CNA's GlProfile layer, not through the tier.

target.evidence: meta-gl@20c8b2dc:include/metagl/DesktopEsTier.hpp (file comment); grep DesktopEsTier in modules/ at 009d40f5 = 0 hits; modules/renderers/easygl/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/EasyGL/GlProfile.hpp

concepts.note: The unit presents the tier as the mechanism that lets OPENGL33 share one implementation; it is a diagnostic.

concepts.section: Device initialization delegates context truth downward
concepts.text: After detection easy-gl requires five baseline features (VertexArrayObject, Shader, Program, Buffer, BasicRendering); a missing one throws during initialization rather than failing later.

concepts.section: Device initialization delegates context truth downward
concepts.text: Optional entry points (queries, samplers, transform feedback, sync objects, program pipelines, texture level-parameter queries) are checked with metagl::IsFunctionAvailable() and fail with easygl::UnsupportedFeatureException instead of calling a null function pointer.

target.evidence: easy-gl@deda7a42:src/Query.cpp, Sampler.cpp, TransformFeedback.cpp, Sync.cpp, ProgramPipeline.cpp, Texture.cpp (IsFunctionAvailable guards)

concepts.section: Device initialization delegates context truth downward
concepts.text: WebGL 1 may obtain vertex arrays only through GL_OES_vertex_array_object (initialisation throws without it below 3.0), and separable program pipelines have no WebGL equivalent at all, WebGL 2 included.
tokens: permanently absent from WebGL 1 and WebGL 2

concepts.section: Capability gating by feature, not version
concepts.text: easygl::Capabilities::detect_common_features() is a per-feature gating table, not a single 'desktop versus ES' branch; WebGL is routed through the ES rules so features WebGL never has fall out of the same checks.

concepts.section: Capability gating by feature, not version
concepts.text: Vertex array objects need GL 3.0 or GL_ARB_vertex_array_object on desktop, but ES 3.0 or the differently named GL_OES_vertex_array_object on ES and WebGL.

concepts.section: Capability gating by feature, not version
concepts.text: Framebuffer objects need GL 3.0 or an ARB/EXT extension on desktop but are always present on ES 2.0 and above, because FBOs are core in ES 2.0.

concepts.section: Capability gating by feature, not version
concepts.text: Tessellation shaders need desktop GL 4.0 but only ES 3.2, a case where the ES requirement is numerically lower; Direct State Access (desktop 4.5) is never set for ES, and an unset feature answers false.

concepts.section: Capability gating by feature, not version
concepts.text: Device::supports(Feature) answers from the table and Device::require(Feature) throws UnsupportedFeatureException when the feature is missing and Config::throw_on_missing_feature is true (the default); with false it returns silently.

concepts.section: Capability gating by feature, not version
concepts.text: CNA's EasyGL renderer does not gate features through Device::supports/require at 009d40f5: it contains no easygl::Feature query or require() call and instead reads capabilities().is_webgl()/is_opengl(), the version string, metagl::IsFunctionAvailable("glColorMaski") and its own live-context probes.
concepts.note: The unit says CNA relies on device.supports()/device.require(); that is not true at the snapshot.

concepts.section: Meta-gl's typed call surface and invalid-input contract
concepts.text: meta-gl exports 358 numbered metagl::gl* wrappers; tools/verify_api.py fails unless the markers are the contiguous range 1..358 with unique names, and it cross-checks the exact mandatory sets added by GLES 2.0/3.0/3.1/3.2 (142/104/68/44) against the vendored Khronos header.

concepts.section: Meta-gl's typed call surface and invalid-input contract
concepts.text: meta-gl's type vocabulary is 105 enum classes in Enums.hpp and 16 structs in Types.hpp (eleven object handles, UniformLocation, AttribLocation, ActiveAttribIndex, ImageUnit, GlBitfieldTraits); older counts of 99 enums and 15 structs are stale.

concepts.section: Meta-gl's typed call surface and invalid-input contract
concepts.text: meta-gl handles are ownership-free values: metagl::TextureId{rawName} neither creates nor deletes the GL name; easygl::Texture owns that lifetime.

concepts.section: Meta-gl's typed call surface and invalid-input contract
concepts.text: The layers fail differently: easy-gl throws C++ exceptions for unsupported features, while meta-gl's invalid-input contract calls std::terminate(), also in Release, for a size_t that does not fit GLsizei, incomplete matrix data or an unsupported bitfield.
concepts.note: Extension on the page: every meta-gl wrapper also terminates when called uninitialised or with an unloaded entry point (372 std::terminate() sites).

concepts.section: Meta-gl's typed call surface and invalid-input contract
concepts.text: Because easy-gl throws, its Emscripten build needs one exception ABI for every object including meta-gl; since easy-gl deda7a42 the model is the cache variable EASYGL_EMSCRIPTEN_EXCEPTION_MODEL (WASM default = -fwasm-exceptions, or JS), and CNA forces JS to match its JS-lowered exception ABI plus Asyncify.

target.evidence: easy-gl@deda7a42:cmake/EasyGlPlatform.cmake; cmake/RendererSelection.cmake (FORCE JS under EMSCRIPTEN); cmake/BuildPerformance.cmake; CNA commit dccfb88f8

concepts.note: The unit says easy-gl enables -fwasm-exceptions globally; that was true up to 0b46d35c only.

concepts.section: Meta-gl's typed call surface and invalid-input contract
concepts.text: meta-gl's binary discipline is strict for 12 headers: hidden visibility with a METAGL_API export macro, a GNU/Clang version script, SONAME and exported-symbol policy tests and an installed-package consumer test.

concepts.section: Meta-gl's typed call surface and invalid-input contract
concepts.text: meta-gl is found as find_package(meta-gl 0.3): project version 0.3.0, and for 0.x releases only the same minor version is compatible.

concepts.section: Meta-gl's typed call surface and invalid-input contract
concepts.text: An uncommitted 0.4.0-snapshot VERSION file once present in a local meta-gl worktree is not a released or pinned version.
concepts.note: The local meta-gl worktree is clean at 20c8b2dc and has no VERSION file; the file was never committed, so there is nothing current to document.

concepts.section: Design corrections and one breaking change
concepts.text: Program::uniform_block_index() returns std::optional<unsigned int> instead of GL's raw GL_INVALID_INDEX sentinel, so failure is tested without a GL header.

concepts.section: Design corrections and one breaking change
concepts.text: Framebuffer attach functions take const Texture& or const Renderbuffer& (and ProgramPipeline/TransformFeedback take const Program&) instead of raw unsigned handles, turning a wrong-handle mistake into a compile error.

concepts.section: Design corrections and one breaking change
concepts.text: Breaking change: Device::clear() used to disable the scissor test before every clear; it now only builds the mask and calls glClear, so callers relying on the implicit disable must call set_scissor_test_enabled(false). CNA's own Clear saves and restores scissor and colour masks for XNA semantics.

concepts.section: Four focused RAII additions
concepts.text: ScopedDebugGroup pushes a labelled debug group in its constructor and always pops it in its destructor, so capture regions stay balanced across early returns and exceptions; it does no availability check.

concepts.section: Four focused RAII additions
concepts.text: UniformCache memoises uniform locations by name, including failed lookups (-1), so a wrong name is never re-queried; only invalidate(), required after a relink, clears it; it holds a raw const Program* that must outlive it.

concepts.section: Four focused RAII additions
concepts.text: ScopedBind generalises the pattern to any bind/unbind pair: the first callable runs in the constructor, the second is stored in a std::function and always runs in the destructor.

concepts.section: Four focused RAII additions
concepts.text: ResourceRegistration calls registry.add(&resource) in its constructor and registry.remove(&resource) in its destructor, so a recoverable resource cannot leave a dangling pointer in its registry.
concepts.note: CNA uses none of the four helpers at 009d40f5; it calls ResourceRegistry::add/remove directly.

concepts.section: Two tiers of context-loss recovery
concepts.text: Tier one of context-loss handling is free detection: eleven integer-handle classes derive from easygl::detail::GenerationTracked, which stamps the meta-gl context generation at creation and answers is_valid_for_current_generation().

concepts.section: Two tiers of context-loss recovery
concepts.text: Sync is the exception to tier one: its handle is a pointer-shaped GLsync, it does not derive from GenerationTracked and only offers its own reset, so it can discard a stale handle but not answer the generation query.

concepts.section: Two tiers of context-loss recovery
concepts.text: reset_handle_no_gl() zeroes the handle and generation without issuing any GL call, because a lost context cannot be trusted with one.

concepts.section: Two tiers of context-loss recovery
concepts.text: Tier two is opt-in rebuilding: RecoverableResource's release_gl_handle_only()/recreate_gl_resource() pair is driven by ResourceRegistry, a metagl::ContextListener that receives loss/restore notifications once register_with_meta_gl() is called, calling each resource in registration order.

concepts.section: Two tiers of context-loss recovery
concepts.text: Implementing tier two means a resource must keep enough CPU-side state (pixels, shader source, buffer contents) to rebuild its GPU object, not merely notice a stale handle.

concepts.section: Two tiers of context-loss recovery
concepts.text: No easy-gl production class implements RecoverableResource, but the mechanism is not unused: at 009d40f5 ten CNA classes (EasyGLRenderer and its texture, render-target, cube, query, GPU-timer, sprite-batch, vertex- and index-buffer renderers) derive from ::easygl::RecoverableResource.
concepts.note: The unit says only tier one is used by anything real; CNA is a real tier-two adopter.

concepts.section: Two tiers of context-loss recovery
concepts.text: easy-gl tests tier two with a test-only FakeResource stub in test_resource_registry_context_lost and test_resource_registry_wired_to_meta_gl because no production easy-gl class adopts it.

concepts.section: Two tiers of context-loss recovery
concepts.text: For a plain easy-gl client, context loss is cheaply detectable per resource but nothing rebuilds a lost Texture or Buffer automatically: detect through tier one and rebuild by hand, or write a RecoverableResource around your own CPU data.

target.evidence: easy-gl@deda7a42:include/easygl/*.hpp (no RecoverableResource in any resource class)

concepts.section: Testing without a GPU
concepts.text: easy-gl has four hand-rolled mock-loader test executables, easy-gl-smoke-tests, easy-gl-resource-smoke-tests, easy-gl-context-lifecycle-tests and easy-gl-webgl-tests.

concepts.section: Testing without a GPU
concepts.text: Fake GetProcAddress loaders return hard-wired callbacks with literal version strings and enum values, so detection and resource bookkeeping run without any GPU or display.
concepts.note: Literal strings at deda7a42 are "3.3.0 easy-gl stub", "OpenGL ES 3.1" and a WebGL 1 string rather than the unit's example.

concepts.section: Testing without a GPU
concepts.text: The lifecycle suite drives loss and restore; the WebGL suite checks explicit classification, ES2/ES3 tiers, OES vertex-array gating and exception-not-crash behaviour of unavailable entry points.

concepts.section: Testing without a GPU
concepts.text: The two desktop-shaped suites are not built under Emscripten because their invented desktop version strings cannot come from a browser; that is a test-model boundary, not evidence that browser behaviour was executed.

concepts.section: Testing without a GPU
concepts.text: Nested defaults are asymmetric: easy-gl defaults EASYGL_BUILD_TESTS and EASYGL_BUILD_EXAMPLES ON, CNA sets both OFF only in its web preset, and neither CNA's root CMake nor renderer selection forces them, so other GL configurations compile easy-gl's test executables.
concepts.note: Whether the easy-gl add_test registrations appear in CNA-root ctest was not established (not configured).

concepts.section: Testing without a GPU
concepts.text: easy-gl's SDL hello-triangle example is added only when find_package(SDL3 QUIET) finds a package; CNA's NPV-0114 record shows it once picked up a /usr/local SDL3 in a CNA_ENABLE_SDL=OFF build, which is why CNA now disables SDL find_package lookups when SDL is off.
concepts.note: The unit says the example can configure because CNA already supplies SDL; CNA supplies targets, while the example looks for a package.

concepts.section: Testing without a GPU
concepts.text: meta-gl defaults all tests, GPU tests, examples, docs, sanitizers and debug options OFF, honouring legacy aliases only when top-level; its standalone suite adds compile, mock-loader, release-contract, thread, desktop-tier, SONAME, export-symbol, API-consistency and installed-package tests, an opt-in EGL/Mesa smoke test, and requesting GPU tests without ordinary tests is a FATAL_ERROR.

concepts.section: Two known, honestly stated limitations
concepts.text: Config::enable_debug_logging does nothing because Config has no log_callback to receive output (Config::validate_calls is likewise never read).

target.evidence: easy-gl@deda7a42:include/easygl/Config.hpp; NEXT.md (S1/S2 incomplete); git grep enable_debug_logging src = 0

concepts.section: Two known, honestly stated limitations
concepts.text: Query::result_u64() reads with the 32-bit glGetQueryObjectuiv and widens the value because meta-gl exposes no 64-bit query read, so results above UINT32_MAX cannot be returned.

concepts.section: Two known, honestly stated limitations
concepts.text: The 32-bit limit reaches CNA: EasyGLGpuTimerRenderer reads GL_TIME_ELAPSED nanoseconds 32-bit (saturating a little above 4.29 seconds), cannot ask GL_GPU_DISJOINT_EXT through meta-gl, and rejects the all-ones 0xFFFFFFFF value as unavailable.
